current_draft.content_markdown:
RIYADH, Saudi Arabia — Usetech said it will present its operational technology portfolio at LEAP 2026 in Riyadh, exhibiting a set of products and integrated solutions tailored to organisations building digital infrastructure, managing operational systems, and applying AI across industrial and urban environments. The company will be on stand H3.B170 in Hall 3 during the event, which runs from August 31 to September 3. Usetech’s announcement positions the firm as a contributor to the operational technology (OT) narrative at a show that has traditionally focused on software, startups and large-scale digital transformation projects.

## What Usetech will showcase

At the centre of Usetech’s stand is Launch, an AI-driven platform for multimodal data analytics. Launch is designed to ingest and correlate diverse data streams — such as sensor telemetry, video, and log files — so operators and analysts can surface contextual insights from converged datasets. The company says the platform targets complex operational environments where decisions rely on understanding signals from multiple sources in near real time.

Complementing Launch is Octopus, described as a universal platform for AI-based IT resource optimisation in data centres. Octopus aims to automate allocation and scheduling of compute, storage and network resources to match fluctuating workloads, an approach intended to address the growing infrastructure pressure from large-scale AI deployments and other data-intensive applications. Usetech will also display Teal HR, an employee motivation platform intended to support workforce engagement during technology transitions; Smart City solutions focused on civilian policing and critical infrastructure protection; and a Smart Manufacturing portfolio that the company positions as an end-to-end offering for connecting machines and systems across production environments.

The selection of products reflects a deliberate OT angle: rather than focusing solely on cloud-native applications or business software, Usetech’s suite ties analytics, resource management and workplace tools directly to physical operations. The company will demonstrate these integrations at LEAP through use cases and product showcases intended for operators, systems integrators and infrastructure managers.

## Relevance for industrial and urban operators

Usetech’s portfolio addresses three intersecting needs in industrial and urban settings: situational awareness, resource efficiency and workforce alignment. Smart City offerings target municipal requirements such as monitoring of critical assets and support for civilian policing functions, where combining video analytics, sensor feeds and command-and-control workflows can enhance response and oversight. The company presents these capabilities as tools for authorities and utilities that must balance safety, service continuity and regulatory constraints.

For manufacturers and production facilities, the Smart Manufacturing portfolio is presented as a bridge between legacy equipment and modern edge and cloud systems. By enabling machine-to-system connectivity and data flow, the portfolio is intended to help factories improve visibility into operations and support predictive maintenance and automation initiatives. Usetech frames these capabilities as foundational for Industry 4.0 projects that typically require orchestration across control systems, IT networks and analytics platforms.

In data centre environments, Octopus targets the technical challenge of matching finite infrastructure to variable demand, especially as enterprises host more AI workloads that can be highly resource-intensive. Efficient management of compute and storage can affect operational costs and service levels; Octopus is positioned to provide automated policies and optimisation routines to help administrators balance those trade-offs. Across all verticals, the reliance on multimodal analytics and integrated control highlights the practical intersection of OT and IT, where interoperability and end-to-end data flows matter for both performance and governance.

## Integration, deployment and regional context

Usetech’s presence at LEAP 2026 comes against a backdrop of significant investment in digital infrastructure across the Middle East, notably in Saudi Arabia’s smart city and industrial modernisation initiatives. The company’s exhibit aims to engage partners and customers evaluating how to deploy OT solutions that must coexist with existing control systems, bespoke operational processes and local regulatory regimes. Usetech acknowledges that practical implementation requires careful system integration, tailored configurations and an execution plan that accounts for operational risk and continuity.

Key considerations for buyers include interoperability with legacy equipment, data governance and cybersecurity. Connecting operational assets to analytics platforms increases the attack surface and raises questions about segmentation, access control and incident response. Usetech’s demonstrations at LEAP will likely be used to discuss integration strategies, deployment roadmaps and the technical controls necessary to meet industry-specific compliance requirements.

Workforce readiness is another deployment dimension. Tools such as Teal HR reflect a recognition that technology adoption often succeeds or fails based on human factors: training, change management and ongoing support. Usetech positions employee engagement capabilities as complementary to its technical offerings, intended to help organisations align personnel with new workflows and performance expectations.

LEAP provides a forum where vendors, system integrators and end users can examine these practicalities. Usetech’s exhibition offers a chance to move beyond product descriptions to operational scenarios that demonstrate how multimodal analytics, resource optimisation and connected manufacturing systems operate together in controlled settings. For procurement and operations teams, such demonstrations can surface integration challenges, clarifying the technical and organisational steps required to realise value.

While Usetech’s products are aimed at improving decision-making and resource efficiency, the company and potential customers will need to evaluate each solution against site-specific constraints — from regulatory limits on data sharing to the realities of equipment lifecycles and capital planning. Demonstrations at LEAP will likely focus on prototype integrations and reference architectures that can be adapted to local use cases rather than one-size-fits-all deployments.

Usetech’s exhibition at stand H3.B170 underlines the company’s intent to be part of the regional OT conversation. By presenting a portfolio that spans analytics, infrastructure optimisation, workforce engagement and sector-specific solutions for cities and manufacturing, the firm frames the operational technology conversation around practical integration challenges. As LEAP convenes technology providers and buyers, Usetech’s participation will signal how vendors are packaging OT capabilities for markets that are actively investing in digital infrastructure and smarter operations.
